styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's tile density is on par with the references: 18 visible tones per tile against 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well, with 0% near-flat coverage. That density comes mostly from the small bottles and jars on the shelves. The cabinet frame is a pale body with only about 3 lightness steps (white, light grey, grey), where Beodeul materials use 5-6. All of its dark edge pixels (100%) are neutral, so the outline is a uniform grey-black line around the frame instead of the dark tone of the adjacent material. The tinted references (hedge 0%, cheese stall 1%) show the Beodeul alternative. The result reads as a sticker-like cabinet with a neutral outline and shallow body shading. The lamp-crook reference is also 100% neutral, but it is a thin metal prop, so it does not justify a neutral outline on a large furniture body.
